source: Hand-coded from English Wikipedia articles, read on 2026-11-13. Each row links the article its claim comes from.
licence: Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0. The evidence lines are our own summaries.
note: Not a dataset: 14 countries sorted by hand into hands, chopsticks or cutlery, one row each, only where a Wikipedia article says plainly how most people there eat. Countries are not one thing (the India article itself says cutlery is common in parts of the country), and a country missing here just means we found no clear line to cite. style 'cutlery' covers both knife and fork and spoon and fork; utensils says which.

countries.evidence: Says most Indians eat with their hands with minimal cutlery, while cutlery is common in some parts.

Says Moroccans traditionally eat with their hands and use bread.
Says the Burmese traditionally eat with their right hand; chopsticks and spoons are for noodle dishes.
